maria gomez: Ran the long-context quant bakeoff this morning. Focus: SmoothQuant + activation-aware AWQ vs GPTQ (INT8/FP8) on redwood-30b with 64k context. Posting quick artifacts and suggested deployment fallback profile.

alex chen: Nice — did you include KV-cache stress (many prefixes + mid-sequence regen)?

maria gomez: yes, 3 patterns: (1) prefix-heavy chat (50k prefix + 5k generation), (2) sliding-window summarization, (3) synthetic long unbatched queries to hit KV eviction.

samir patel: command you ran?

maria gomez: ```
# run on bench cluster (gpu-pool-d)
python tools/quant_eval.py \
  --model redwood-30b-rlhf \n  --quant awq --smoothquant \n  --ctx 65536 --batch 1 \n  --dataset longbench_v2 --tasks qa,summarize,perplexity \n  --seeds 42 --save artifacts/1901203333/

python tools/quant_eval.py \n  --model redwood-30b-rlhf \n  --quant gptq --bits 8 --ctx 65536 --batch 1 \n  --dataset longbench_v2 --save artifacts/1901203333/gptq/
```

maria gomez: TL;DR results (median over 3 runs):
- AWQ+SmoothQuant (activation-aware int8): QA F1 drop: -1.8 pts, Summarize ROUGE-L -1.5 pts, Perplexity +6% vs fp32. P95 token latency: 210ms.
- GPTQ int8 (no act-aware): QA F1 drop: -4.5 pts, ROUGE-L -3.9 pts, Perplexity +18%. P95 token latency: 200ms.
- FP8 variant (mixed FP8 kernels): QA F1 drop: -0.9 pts, ROUGE-L -0.6 pts, Perplexity +2.7%. P95 token latency: 260ms.

NOTE: AWQ gave better quality than GPTQ for long-context despite small latency tradeoff. FP8 best quality but is slower and has larger memory footprint for some kernels.

dina kozlowski: interesting that AWQ latency is similar to GPTQ. Did you hit different kernel paths?

maria gomez: yes — AWQ + smoothquant forces some extra pre/post scaling and a small relayout for activations on 80% of layers; that increases per-token overhead slightly but preserves distribution. On our A100 pools it maps to the same continuous-batch kernel family as GPTQ for the decoder, so net p95 similar.

samir patel: any failure modes in KV-cache? e.g., evictions causing larger regressions?

maria gomez: we saw drift in the sliding-window scenario when KV eviction occurred aggressively (simulated by tiny cache retention). AWQ had more graceful degradation: the QA drop widened by +0.6pts after repeated eviction cycles for AWQ, but for GPTQ it spiked +2.2pts. FP8 stayed most stable but had ~1.2x memory pressure.

alex chen: do you have artifact paths? want to run locally on devkit.

maria gomez: artifacts: s3://redwood-internal/quant-bakes/1901203333/ (contains logs, eval.csv, per-run .jsonl, kernel trace). Also uploaded a small condensed CSV to the run page.

ci-bot: build 1901203333 completed — artifacts uploaded, bench cluster logs at /var/logs/bench/1901203333.log

dina kozlowski: recommendation for Dedicated deployment?

maria gomez: proposal: default rollout = AWQ+SmoothQuant int8 for longctx routes (>=32k), with two-tier fallback: (1) if p95 latency > 400ms or mempressure > 85% switch to FP8 variant (higher mem, better quality), (2) if tail errors > 0.5% fallback to fp32-safe variant (float32). Canary steps: 5% -> 25% -> 50%. Add deterministic eval hooks (our longbench subset) on every canary step.

samir patel: for Hosted API, I suggest opportunistic fallbacks based on model routing: prefer AWQ unless client requests fp8 or latency SLO violated, then route to fp8 or fp32. Keep billing flag to show when FP8 used.

maria gomez: logged a GH issue with config prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-configs/issues/412 — includes rollout YAML and experiment dashboard links.

alex chen: can you add a quick perf profile for T4 vs A100? customers still on T4 are curious.

maria gomez: yes — next runs scheduled on gpu-pool-c (T4) tonight, I'll post differences. Expect higher p95 and more memory churn; AWQ still likely preferable to GPTQ for quality but may lose the latency edge vs FP8.

dina kozlowski: thanks — let's sync in tomorrow eng-ml stand if numbers on T4 align.
